## About
We're a family owned and operated shop on Greenwood Ave N in Seattle, working on Asian import vehicles. Our owner, Tony, wants to give you an alternative to impersonal and expensive service at dealerships.
When you bring your car in, our service advisor takes your information and notes the service or repairs you need. For most routine services we can give you a price estimate on the spot. If not, we diagnose the problem and get you a quote as soon as we know what's needed. Nothing gets done until we've talked it over with you.
Unlike many shops, we have one technician take care of your car from start to finish. That technician is responsible for the whole job, from the first test drive to the last.
We handle everything from scheduled maintenance to repairs, and we're rated 4.7 from 151 Google reviews. One reviewer called us "a delightful neighborhood auto shop."

## Services
- Factory scheduled maintenance: Routine maintenance done to your car's factory schedule.
- Engine repairs: Diagnosis and repair of engine problems, with a price quote before any work begins.
- Brakes service: Brake inspection and service to keep your car stopping the way it should.
- Cooling system service: Help with overheating and other cooling system problems.
- Buyer and safety inspection: A look over a car you're thinking of buying, or a safety check on the one you already drive.
- Engine and body electrical repairs: Tracking down and fixing electrical problems in the engine and the rest of the car.
- Steering and suspension services: Service and repair for your car's steering and suspension.
- Transmission and clutch services: Service and repair for transmissions and clutches.

## FAQ
Q: What kinds of cars do you work on?
A: We're an Asian import vehicle service and repair shop, and Japanese cars are right there in our name.

Q: How do I make an appointment?
A: You can call us or send an email to schedule, or just come in for any service needs.

Q: When are you open?
A: We're open Monday through Friday and closed on weekends. Our full hours are listed on this page.

Q: Will I know the price before you start?
A: For most routine services we can give you an estimate on the spot. For anything else, we diagnose the problem first and give you a quote as soon as we know what repairs are needed.

Q: Will you do any work without asking me?
A: No. All service and repairs are done only after we've talked with you.

Q: What happens to my car once it's in the shop?
A: One technician follows a 5 step process: an initial test drive if needed, a courtesy check, diagnosis, the repair or service, and a final test drive.

## What customers say
- "In short - Honest, sincere mechanic who isn’t just looking to make a profit, but who thinks just as much about what’s best for you and your car.

My 2007 Toyota Prius needs new struts and shocks. I started calling around for estimates - Tony’s estimate was about $1k less than other places I had called, so I decided to start saving up to go to him. In the meantime, while saving, my car had an unrelated mechanical problem and wasn’t starting while I was parked somewhere I couldn’t stay for long. I decided to call Tony and get his thoughts. He was very patient and helpful, despite not receiving any financial compensation for this very short phone call. He advised me to try a few things before seeing about having it towed to his shop. I called one other local mechanic, to get a second opinion. This second call was notably different - he was polite, but solely focused on getting the car towed to his shop as soon as possible. I really wasn’t looking forward to an unexpected tow bill. After a while, thankfully, the car started up and I was able to drive it home. Although it was just a few minutes on the phone, Tony’s selfless kindness left an impact on me that day.

A few days later, when I was thinking about next steps to getting this problem investigated and fixed, I called Tony again. I wanted to drive it to his shop for a brief inspection, before making the decision to tow it all the way down to Portland, where my car is still on warranty for some large repairs from last year. Instead, he advised me that a brief inspection would be pointless, and it was a better use of my time and money to just take it down to Portland right away. Another shop I called to ask for the same brief inspection here in Seattle before going to Portland was willing to do it. When I called them back and explained Tony’s reason for not scheduling me, they admitted that his reasoning was solid and the inspection was indeed unnecessary.

While I haven’t yet been to Tony’s shop, I can attest that in my brief interactions with him over the phone, he seems like a trustworthy man with good principles." (Erica Taicz-Blandón, 5/5)
